Definition: from a compound of G473 and G5087; opposition, i.e. a conflict (of theories):--opposition.
BiblicalUsage: Paul warns Timothy to avoid profane and vain babblings and oppositions of science falsely so called, the arguments that set themselves against the faith. The word names the conflict of theories, the rival teaching that claims to know better.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for oppositions carries no teaching of its own; its warning is Paul's, that clever arguments dressed as knowledge can shipwreck the faith.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
